cities.name: Jagdalpur
cities.overview: The main town of the Bastar region, a base for waterfalls, cave systems and the tribal haats (weekly markets) of southern Chhattisgarh.

cities.name: Kawardha
cities.overview: A small town in Kabirdham district at the foot of the Maikal hills, about 120 km from Raipur.

places.name: Chitrakote Falls
places.shortDescription: India's widest waterfall, where the Indravati River drops in a horseshoe curve, often called the Niagara of India.
places.description: At Chitrakote the Indravati River plunges about 29 m over a horseshoe-shaped cliff that can stretch roughly 300 m wide in the monsoon. The falls change character through the year, from a roaring red-brown curtain in August to separate silvery streams in the dry season. Boats take visitors close to the base when the water is calm, and viewpoints on the rim catch the evening light. A small Shiva temple stands near the edge.
places.history: The falls lie in Bastar, a region of Gond, Muria and other Adivasi communities whose festivals, such as the 75-day Bastar Dussehra, are among India's most distinctive.
places.bestTimeNote: July to October for full flow; November to February for boat rides and pleasant weather.

places.name: Kanger Valley National Park
places.shortDescription: Sal forests, limestone caves and the Tirathgarh waterfall in a compact national park near Jagdalpur.
places.description: Kanger Valley (Kanger Ghati) National Park follows the Kanger River through dense sal and teak forest. Its best-known sights are Kotumsar Cave, an underground passage of stalactites and blind fish reached by narrow steps, and the tiered Tirathgarh waterfall. The park is also home to the hill myna, the state bird, which mimics human speech. Guides are required inside the caves and the caves close during the monsoon.
places.history: The area was declared a national park in 1982 and takes its name from the Kanger River that runs through it.
places.bestTimeNote: November to April. The park and caves are usually closed in the monsoon (July to October).

entryFee.note: Park entry, vehicle and cave fees are charged separately; guides are mandatory in the caves.

location.address: Kanger Ghati National Park, Darbha, Bastar district, Chhattisgarh

places.name: Bhoramdeo Temple
places.shortDescription: An 11th-century Shiva temple in the Maikal hills, covered in sculpture and often called the Khajuraho of Chhattisgarh.
places.description: Set beside a lake at the foot of the Maikal hills, the Bhoramdeo Temple is a Nagara-style Shiva temple whose outer walls are carved with deities, dancers and amorous couples in the manner of Khajuraho. A few kilometres away are the smaller Madwa Mahal and the brick Cherki Mahal. The surroundings are peaceful and see few outside visitors. A local festival is held here in March.
places.history: The temple is attributed to the Nagavanshi rulers of the region and is generally dated to the late 11th century CE.
